_meta.schema_notes: All *_weights and *weight* fields are fractions summing to ~1.0 within their group and are meant to be sampled directly (e.g. weighted random choice). Percentile fields describe the *value* distribution shape for numeric sampling (e.g. log-normal-ish interpolation between percentiles).

locations.note_pseudo_qty_is_cumulative: For rows whose Location(qty) includes ONLY real (non-pseudo) locations, the summed quantities equal Quantity On Hand in 99.9% of cases (3621/3625). When a pseudo-location (dispatched/trash/loss/process/recycle/In Transit) is present, the summed quantities usually EXCEED Quantity On Hand by a large margin -- these pseudo-location counts are ALL-TIME CUMULATIVE dispatched/trashed/lost counts, not current stock. Do not treat Location(qty) as a simple partition of Quantity On Hand once a pseudo-location appears.

primary_scheme.note: Numeric value increases monotonically with Inventoried date (nearly sequential allocation) -- IDs from 2026 rows cluster at the top of the range.

legacy_letter_prefixed.pattern: single letter prefix + digits, occasional Q suffix (+ optional 2-digit split number)
legacy_letter_prefixed.note: Legacy IDs from an older inventory scheme (pre-~2020), still lingering because the items have never been dispatched/removed. Not seen after 2020 in this snapshot.

q_suffix.meaning_guess: quantity-split / child record of an original inventory number

date_distribution.note: Heavy right-skew: 58.5% of all rows dated in 2026 (the current year of the snapshot), rising month-on-month through the year (Aug and Sep 2026 are the two busiest months). Pre-2021 rows are almost entirely the legacy letter-prefixed inventory numbers.

dimension_rules.cbm_formula: CBM = (Length_cm * Width_cm * Height_cm) / 1,000,000 -- verified exact (ratio 1.00 median, no deviation) on all 3,840 rows where L, W, H and CBM are all present. Generator should COMPUTE CBM, never sample it independently.
dimension_rules.units: Length/Width/Height in cm, Weight in kg, Value in HKD (implied, unlabelled), CBM in cubic metres.

description_style.leading_space_note: Nearly every description (96.4%) starts with a single leading space, an artifact of the source system -- generator should replicate this.
description_style.cross_reference_pattern: Furniture/matched-set items sometimes reference another inventory number in the description, e.g. "Matches #059856", "(matches armchair #128746)" -- a small but real pattern for paired/matched furniture sets.
description_style.destination_tag_pattern: A leading "FOR <TAG>" (all-caps) block is used for earmarked shipments/programs, e.g. "FOR HKD" (Hong Kong Distribution), "FOR TAIPO", "FOR MOLDOVA", "FOR S1358" (shipment/container ref) -- these are program/place codes, not addresses.
